title: Meeting Kuih, Birthday Cake and Free Food at the Office: How to Handle It
intro: You don't have to say no to all meeting kuih or birthday cake to lose weight. What helps is choosing mindfully, taking small portions and not eating just because it's free.

sections.h: Count how often it really happens
sections.p: One karipap is an estimated 130-150 kcal, a piece of seri muka an estimated 150-200 kcal, and a slice of birthday cake can be an estimated 300-450 kcal. Once in a while is no problem. But if there's meeting kuih almost every day, it can add up and slow down your progress.

sections.h: Pick the one you like most
sections.p: Instead of taking a bit of everything, pick one kuih you really like. Put it on a plate, sit down and eat slowly. Eating while answering emails usually makes us take more without realising.

Join the celebration, sing and take photos. Ask for a small slice or share with a friend. If you're not hungry, you can pack it and eat it when you really want to, not because everyone else is eating.
No need to explain your diet to everyone. Just say 'Thanks, I just ate' or 'I'll take this one first, okay'. Smile, and change the topic. Most people won't even notice.

action: This week, limit meeting kuih to one piece per meeting.
Eat a lunch with enough protein so afternoon kuih isn't too tempting.
Prepare one polite line for saying no that you're comfortable using.
Bring your own water or kopi o to meetings so your hands have something to hold.
When there's free food, ask yourself first: if this wasn't free, would I buy it?
myth: Some believe that once you've eaten one kuih, the day is ruined so you might as well eat everything. Actually, one kuih doesn't erase your effort, what matters is your next choice and your pattern across the week.

faq.q: I feel awkward saying no to food my boss treats us to. What should I do?
faq.a: Take a little and say thank you. You can eat half and keep the rest. Appreciating a treat doesn't mean you have to finish all of it.

faq.q: I ate too much kuih today, should I skip dinner?
faq.a: No need. Skipping meals usually makes you hungrier and overeat the next day. Have dinner as usual with protein and vegetables, and carry on with your routine.

faq.q: Do I need to exercise for a long time to burn off one kuih?
faq.a: Don't think of food as something you have to pay for with exercise. Exercise is great for health and strength, while your body weight is influenced more by your daily eating pattern.
